<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 1 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Wonderful Wizard of Oz ==

The Tin Woodman, also known simply as the Woodman, is a companion of Dorothy on her journey along the road of yellow brick toward the Emerald City, traveling alongside the Scarecrow and, later, the Cowardly Lion and the dog Toto. He admits to never having been to the Emerald City himself, though his father made the journey once when he was a boy and reported it as long and passing through dangerous country, growing more beautiful nearer the city where Oz dwells. The Woodman knows that he has no heart, and for that reason takes great care never to be cruel or unkind to anything, walking carefully so as not to even harm a passing ant; as he puts it, those with hearts have something to guide them, but having none, he must be especially careful.

His care extends to protecting his companions and the creatures around him: he holds Toto back from chasing the field mice, refuses to kill a deer for food for fear that weeping over it would rust his jaws, and carries an oil-can to keep his joints moving. He performs much of the group's practical labor, chopping wood for their camp with his axe and building the raft of logs and wooden pins used to cross a wide river that blocked their path, standing at one end with the Scarecrow to steady it with long poles. When a great Wildcat comes bounding after a small mouse who turns out to be the Queen of the Field Mice, he kills the beast with his axe, and afterward helps push the mice's truck to safety. His head, which turns on hinges, and his tin body serve him well: when the Scarecrow later scatters his own straw over Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion to shield them from the Wicked Witch's bees, the bees find only the Woodman to sting and break all their stingers against his tin without harming him at all.

=== Events ===

* They discover a rusted Tin Woodman standing motionless with an axe raised, mid-chop on a tree.
* The Tin Woodman thanks them for saving his life and asks to join their journey to see Oz.
* The group continues down the yellow brick road, with the Tin Woodman clearing overgrown branches with his axe.
* The Tin Woodman recounts his backstory: an enchanted axe cursed by the Wicked Witch of the East cut off his limbs and head one by one, each replaced with tin by a tinsmith, until he lost his body and finally his heart.
* A great Lion leaps out, knocks over the Scarecrow, and claws at the Tin Woodman without effect.
* The Tin Woodman suggests the Lion's fear may be heart disease, noting he himself has no heart at all.
* Each companion states a wish for Oz: brains for the Scarecrow, a heart for the Woodman, return to Kansas for Dorothy.
* Later the Tin Woodman accidentally kills a beetle, weeps in remorse, and his tears rust his jaw shut until the Scarecrow oils him.
* Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion camp overnight under a tree, with Dorothy sharing the last of her bread while the Scarecrow gathers nuts for her.
* They come to a second, wider ditch and the Tin Woodman chops down a tree to form a bridge across it.
* Two Kalidahs pursue them across the fallen tree, but the Tin Woodman chops away the end of the tree, sending the beasts crashing to their deaths in the ditch below.
* In the afternoon they arrive at a broad river with a beautiful country visible on the far bank, and the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.
* The travelers cross the river on a raft the Tin Woodman built, but the current sweeps them off course.
* The poppies' scent overpowers Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion, putting them to sleep, while the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman remain unaffected.
* The Scarecrow and Tin Woodman carry the sleeping Dorothy out of the poppies to safety, forced to leave the Lion behind.
* The Tin Woodman kills a Wildcat that was chasing a small field mouse, cutting off its head with his axe.
* The rescued mouse reveals she is the Queen of the Field Mice and thanks the Woodman for saving her life.
* The Queen orders all field mice to serve the Woodman and obey him for his brave deed.
* Toto tries to chase the gathered mice, but the Woodman restrains him and assures the frightened Queen he will not be allowed to bite.
* The Queen summons thousands of mice with pieces of string while the Woodman builds a wooden truck from tree limbs.
* The Tin Woodman sees Oz as a monstrous five-limbed Beast, and the Lion sees Oz as a Ball of Fire; both are told the same condition for a heart and courage.
* The Wicked Witch spots the travelers and sends a pack of forty wolves to destroy them, but the Tin Woodman kills them all with his axe.
* The Witch sends a swarm of black bees to sting them, but the Scarecrow has his straw spread over his friends while the bees break their stings against the Woodman's tin body.
* The Witch uses her Golden Cap's third and final charm to summon the Winged Monkeys, who destroy the Scarecrow, batter the Tin Woodman, and capture the Lion.
* The Winkies help Dorothy find the battered, rusted Tin Woodman and carry him back to the Yellow Castle.
* Tinsmiths spend three days and four nights straightening, soldering, and mending the Tin Woodman back into shape.
* A Winkie goldsmith fits the Woodman's axe with a new golden handle and polishes the blade.
* The group locates the tree holding the Scarecrow's clothes, and the Tin Woodman chops it down to free them.
* Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion get lost in the fields of buttercups and daisies while trying to walk back to the Emerald City.
* The Winged Monkeys carry Dorothy, Toto, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion through the air to the gates of the Emerald City.
* The Tin Woodman goes to Oz to receive his promised heart.
* Oz cuts a hole in the Woodman's tin chest and inserts a silk heart stuffed with sawdust, then solders the patch shut.
* The Tin Woodman asks Dorothy to wipe his tears with a towel so he can mourn Oz without rusting, then oils himself afterward.
* The four companions meet in the Throne Room; the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Lion each express contentment with what they gained from Oz, but Dorothy insists she wants to return to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry in Kansas.
* The Lion, Tin Woodman, and Scarecrow all agree to accompany Dorothy, and the group plans to depart the next morning.
* The Tin Woodman, Scarecrow, and Lion praise Oz, while Dorothy privately forgives him for not keeping his promise.
* The Tin Woodman chops through a branch to clear a path, and the group reaches a high wall of white china beyond the wood.
* The Tin Woodman builds a ladder while Dorothy, the Lion, and Toto rest after their long walk.
* The group sleeps in the forest, with the Woodman and Scarecrow keeping watch.
* Unable to fight the Hammer-Heads, the Tin Woodman suggested summoning the Winged Monkeys, and Dorothy used the Golden Cap one last time.
* Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion tidy themselves before being brought before Glinda, who sits on a throne of rubies.
* Glinda uses the Golden Cap's three remaining commands to send the Winged Monkeys to carry the Scarecrow to the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman to the Winkies, and the Lion to his forest.
</div>

== The Marvelous Land of Oz ==

Nick Chopper, generally known as the Tin Woodman and called Nick by his companions, rules the West Country of the Winkies, a land where everything is yellow. He was invited to become the Winkies' ruler after he helped Dorothy destroy the Wicked Witch of the West, an act for which the grateful Winkies offered him the throne; he styles himself their Emperor.

Before assuming this rule, Nick Chopper accompanied Dorothy, a girl carried to the Land of Oz from Kansas by a cyclone, and the Scarecrow on her travels through the country. Among his remembered deeds from that period is the destruction of the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves.

When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt drove the Scarecrow from the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman reacted to the news with alarm, calling it a calamity, and resolved to march at once to recapture the city and restore the Scarecrow to his throne. He undertook this journey together with Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, a company later joined along the road by the Woggle-Bug. The march toward the Emerald City was thrown off course when the witch Mombi, summoned by Jinjur to stop the group, worked magic from a tower room that left the Tin Woodman certain they had lost their way despite his knowing every step of the route.

During the journey, the Tin Woodman performed the operation of amputating Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden leg and fitting it, cut down to size, onto the Saw-Horse.

=== Events ===

* The Scarecrow decides to flee to his friend the Tin Woodman, Emperor of the Winkies, for protection.
* The group remounts the Saw-Horse and resumes traveling toward the Tin Woodman, with Jack and the horse bickering along the way.
* Passing familiar landmarks, the Scarecrow recalls earlier adventures with Dorothy, including the Stinging Bees, the Grey Wolves defeated by Nick Chopper (the Tin Woodman), and their capture by the Winged Monkeys.
* The Scarecrow explains that the Tin Woodman (Nick Chopper) was made Emperor of the Winkies after the Wicked Witch's destruction.
* The Tin Woodman rushes out to embrace the Scarecrow, accidentally smearing him with polishing paste.
* The Tin Woodman welcomes Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, and explains the engraved star on his chest covers the patch where the Wizard placed his heart.
* Learning the rebels plan to march on the Winkie palace too, the Tin Woodman decides to help retake the Emerald City without needing a large army.
* General Jinjur, fearing the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman joining forces against her rebel army, sends for the witch Mombi to stop their return to the Emerald City.
* The Tin Woodman realizes the group has gone astray and they find themselves surrounded by a field of giant sunflowers with girls' faces, which they suspect is Mombi's illusion.
* Nick Chopper amputates Jack's left leg and fits it to the Saw-Horse, prompting bickering between Jack and the Saw-Horse before the group resumes travel toward the Emerald City.
* The Tin Woodman chops down the Saw-Horse's new leg because it is too long, letting the wooden horse walk more comfortably.
* The Woggle-Bug argues that puns display superior education, irritating Tip and drawing a warning from the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to restrain himself.
* The Tin Woodman blows a silver whistle to summon the Queen of the Field Mice, an old friend whose life he once saved.
* The travelers, led by the Tin Woodman wielding his axe, frighten off the Army of Revolt guards and enter the Emerald City unopposed.
* Jinjur signals the Army of Revolt, who surround and disarm the group, seizing the Tin Woodman's axe and taking them prisoner.
* After thinking quietly, the Scarecrow proposes building a flying machine on the roof and using the Powder of Life to animate it, with the Tin Woodman as builder.
* The Tin Woodman repairs Jack Pumpkinhead's broken leg with a table leg, and the group disperses to gather materials for the aerial machine.
* The adventurers gather assorted objects on the palace roof: a Gump's head with antlers, two sofas, a broom, ropes, and four palm-tree leaves cut by the Tin Woodman.
* The Tin Woodman designs a flying machine, binding two sofas together as a body and attaching the Gump's head to the front.
* The Gump flies south with Tip, Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, Woggle-Bug, and Saw-Horse aboard.
* The travelers fall unharmed into a hidden Jackdaw's nest full of stolen treasures, and the Woggle-Bug gives a found diamond necklace to the Tin Woodman.
* Jackdaws attack the group perched in the Gump's nest, and the Tin Woodman fights them off with his axe while the Saw-Horse kicks with its wooden legs.
* The Tin Woodman, unaware of the rose's true identity, plucks it and pins it to his chest as the search party withdraws in defeat.
* Mombi, disguised as a rose in the Tin Woodman's button-hole, believes herself safe since no one knows the rose and Mombi are the same.
* The Scarecrow and Tin Woodman each propose alternate plans while Glinda notices the rose trembling and suspects it is Mombi in disguise.
* The Tin Woodman prepares to return to the Winkie Country, taking the Scarecrow with him as his Royal Treasurer.
</div>

== Ozma of Oz / A Record of Her Adventures with Dorothy Gale of Kansas, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger; Besides Other Good People too Numerous to Mention Faithfully Recorded Herein ==

The Tin Woodman is a companion of Ozma of Oz, seated among her court alongside the Scarecrow and Tiktok during palace audiences. He commands the Army of Oz, describing it as composed of eight Generals, six Colonels, seven Majors, five Captains, and a small handful of privates. He takes part in Ozma's processions, marching side by side with Tiktok just behind the Scarecrow. According to Billina, the Tin Woodman was at one point trapped after Prince Evring accidentally pocketed his enchanted whistle, and was restored the instant it was blown.

=== Events ===

* Ozma leads an expedition of Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, and an army of Oz to free the Queen of Ev and her ten children from the Nome King.
* Ozma fails all eleven guesses and is transformed into an emerald grasshopper; the Tin Woodman, the army officers, and Tiktok are also transformed after failing their own guesses.
* Billina overhears the Nome King reveal that the Ev family are hidden as purple ornaments and the Oz party as green ones, then uses this secret to free everyone except the Tin Woodman.
* Despite the belt's power, the group cannot locate the Tin Woodman and is forced to leave without him, returning to the Land of Ev with the rescued royal family.
* Billina reveals that Prince Evring had accidentally trapped the Tin Woodman by pocketing his enchanted whistle, and blowing it ("Ev") restores him instantly.
* The Tin Woodman is joyfully reunited with the Scarecrow and Tiktok, and the group returns to the royal palace of Ev.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 4 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz ==

The Tin Woodman is remembered fondly as one of the friends of Oz's former Wizard. Skilled with an axe, he once cut a straight, strong limb from a tree and used it to fashion a new leg and ear for the Sawhorse after the Sawhorse was injured. The Wizard treats him as a trusted friend, privately asking him to defend Dorothy's kitten Eureka when she stands accused of eating Princess Ozma's missing piglet. The Tin Woodman also speaks directly to Eureka, warning her that she may be sorry if she continues to act foolishly.

=== Events ===

* In Oz they reunite with the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, and the Woggle-Bug, ending with a race between Jim and the Sawhorse.
* Ozma crowns Sawhorse "Prince of Horses" and Tin Woodman repairs its leg and ear.
* Wizard secretly gives Tin Woodman a duplicate piglet to produce as proof of Eureka's innocence if convicted.
* Jury finds Eureka guilty, but Tin Woodman produces the duplicate piglet, seemingly proving innocence.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 5 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Road to Oz ==

Nick Chopper, known as the Tin Woodman, is a tin man who possesses a heart given to him by the Wizard. After a witch who had enslaved the Winkies was destroyed with a bucket of water, the freed people made Nick Chopper their Emperor. According to Billina, the Tin Woodman's heart grows softer and kindlier every day.

=== Events ===

* The group meets Tik-tok and Billina, who guide them toward the Emerald City and stop overnight at Nick Chopper's tin castle.
* Along the road they visit Jack Pumpkinhead at his pumpkin farm and hear the Tin Woodman's account of the Powder of Life.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Emerald City of Oz ==

Nick Chopper, also known as the Tin Woodman, is a companion of Dorothy and resides in a tin castle in Winkie Country. According to Dorothy, she and the Scarecrow once found him rusted stiff in the woods; after oiling his joints until they were slippery again, he accompanied them to visit the Wizard at the Emerald City. He is counted among the friends the Wizard's party plans to call upon on their travels, alongside Jack Pumpkinhead and the Scarecrow — of whom the Tin Woodman remarks that their dear Scarecrow cannot be contented with city life however beautiful his surroundings, noting that the Scarecrow originally passed his early life as a farmer in a cornfield, set there to frighten away crows.

During a visit to his tin castle, where his guests toured his tin gardens and fish pond, the Tin Woodman reported that Ozma had seen in her Magic Picture that the Nome King had dug a tunnel under the desert to invade Oz together with the Whimsies, the Growleywogs, and the Phanfasms.

=== Events ===

* The group decides to rest, eat supper, and continue their journey the next day, planning to visit the Rigmaroles and Flutterbudgets before calling on the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Scarecrow.
* The travelers reach Winkie Country and lunch with the Tin Woodman at his tin castle, touring his tin gardens and fish pond.
* The Tin Woodman reveals Ozma saw in her Magic Picture that the Nome King dug a tunnel under the desert to invade Oz alongside the Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms.
</div>

== Narrative role ==

Nick Chopper, known as the Tin Woodman, is met when Tik-tok and Billina guide the travelers toward the Emerald City; the party stops overnight at Nick Chopper's tin castle along the way. The journey later brings them to Jack Pumpkinhead's pumpkin farm, where Nick Chopper recounts his own account of the Powder of Life.

== Personality ==

Nick Chopper's most attested trait is a marked and deepening kindness of heart. Dorothy credits him with "a lovely heart," a gift given to him by the Wizard, and Billina reports that this heart "gets softer and kindlier every day," suggesting an ongoing cultivation of tenderness rather than a fixed disposition. The concern others show for him — Dorothy's eagerness to see him again and her pointed question, "how's his heart?" — reflects the warmth he inspires in his companions.

== Appearance ==

Nick Chopper, also known as the Tin Woodman, is made of tin, a fact reflected in how others refer to him — as "the tin man." No further physical details are given beyond his tin construction.

== Powers ==

Nick Chopper possesses a heart given to him by the Wizard, described as growing "softer and kindlier every day." This heart sets him apart from ordinary beings, marking him as a figure whose inner nature is not fixed at creation but continues to develop over time.

== Trivia ==

* After Dorothy melted the witch who held them captive, the freed people made Nick Chopper their Emp'ror.
* According to Billina, the heart given to Nick Chopper by the Wizard grows softer and kindlier every day.
